changelog.description: New roles, faster switching, and the sign-in security we shipped this season.
changelog.title: See what just shipped

clientPortals.title: A home for every client
clientPortals.summary: Clients can step into their own workspace, review what’s in progress, and leave a note — without borrowing a teammate’s login.

item1.text: Guest access with a view-only role, so clients see progress without a full seat.

item2.text: A client-ready overview on the start page with the work that matters this week.

item3.text: Switching organizations keeps your place, even with a long client list.

planClarity.title: Passkeys and two-factor, built in
planClarity.summary: Signing in should be fast and hard to phish — passkeys and two-factor verification now ship with the starter.

item1.text: Passkey sign-in works out of the box, with no extra configuration.

item2.text: Two-factor verification can be required for accounts that need it.

item3.text: Magic link emails could land in spam with some providers. Delivery is more reliable now.

quietWeek.title: A quieter week of polish
quietWeek.summary: No headline feature — just the empty states, emails, and invite edges that make the product feel finished.

item1.text: Empty members and invitations screens now suggest a next step instead of staring back at you.

item2.text: Invite links failed when the person already had an account. They now drop into the right workspace.

item3.text: Notification emails link straight back to the item that changed, instead of the inbox.

workspaceSwitching.title: Switch workspaces without the wait
workspaceSwitching.summary: Moving between clients should feel like changing folders, not reloading the app. This release is about that click.

item1.text: Organization switching stays snappy even with dozens of memberships.

item2.text: We remember the last workspace you had open and take you back there.

item3.text: The org switcher could show a stale name after a rename. It now follows the workspace.

invites.title: Invites that feel like a handshake
invites.summary: The first email someone gets from PokeDex Manager should name the workspace, the person who asked, and what to do next.

item1.text: Invite emails include the workspace name and who asked you in.

item2.text: First-run setup walks you through creating the first organization instead of dumping you on an empty start page.

item3.text: Expired invites now say so, instead of a generic error.

launch.title: PokeDex Manager, from first login
launch.summary: The first public release: organizations, roles, and secure sign-in in one place — so a team can invite people and get to work without a side quest.

item1.text: Organizations, roles, and secure sign-in live together from day one.

item2.text: A start page for each workspace so teams know where to begin.

item3.text: Passkey and magic-link sign-in ship alongside email and password.

contact.description: Questions about plans, onboarding, or a workspace for your team. We usually reply within one business day.

faq.description: Straight answers to the questions teams ask before they start.
faq.title: Frequently asked questions

dataSecurity.question: Is my Pokédex data secure?
dataSecurity.answer: Yes. Every lab's data is isolated, access is role-based, and you can enable two-factor authentication or passkeys on any account.

inviteTeam.question: Can I invite my research team?
inviteTeam.answer: Yes. Invite researchers by email, assign roles, and everyone stays scoped to their own lab's data.

authMethods.question: What sign-in methods are supported?
authMethods.answer: Email and password, magic links, passkeys, and Google sign-in, with optional two-factor verification.

selfHost.question: Can I self-host PokeDex Manager?
selfHost.answer: Yes. It is a self-hosted Nuxt application — deploy it on your own infrastructure with your own database.

features.title: Everything between your first entry and a full Pokédex
features.description: Opinionated defaults for the hard parts of running a Pokédex platform — so your team can focus on what trainers actually pay for.

feature1.title: Labs and research teams
feature1.subtitle: Invite researchers, manage trainer roles, and keep every lab's Pokédex data isolated from day one.
feature1.description: Multi-tenant structure is built in: create a lab, invite your researchers, and switch between Pokédex projects without custom scaffolding.

benefit1.title: Role-aware access
benefit1.description: Owners, admins, and members get clear permissions out of the box.

benefit2.title: Invites that work
benefit2.description: Email invitations and join flows get new trainers into the lab, not stuck in a demo.

benefit3.title: Active workspace context
benefit3.description: Researchers move between labs without losing their place in the Pokédex.

feature2.title: Secure sign-in for every trainer
feature2.subtitle: Passkeys, two-factor verification, and magic links — without writing your own auth flows.
feature2.description: Google sign-in, passkeys, email and password, and magic links ship out of the box, with two-factor verification for accounts that need it.

benefit1.title: Passkey sign-in
benefit1.description: Trainers sign in with device biometrics — no password required.

benefit2.title: Two-factor verification
benefit2.description: Add a second step for accounts that need it, without extra setup.

benefit3.title: Magic links
benefit3.description: Send a one-time sign-in link straight to a trainer's inbox.

testimonials.title: Trusted by labs cataloging real Pokédex data
testimonials.description: Example quotes you can replace with your own customers once you launch your Pokédex.

item1.quote: We replaced months of auth and security work with a foundation we could actually extend. Our first labs were live and cataloging in weeks, not quarters.
item1.name: Maya Chen

item2.quote: The lab model matched how our research teams already worked. Invites, roles, and switching between Pokédex projects just worked — we spent our time on the product instead.
item2.name: Jonas Weber

item3.quote: Clean defaults, clear structure, and nothing fighting us when we customized our Pokédex. It feels like a senior team left us a strong starting point.
item3.name: Amelia Ortiz
